prior_art_boundary: Wang et al. 2024 already establish a pooled departure-to-arrival carry-over path in spring and autumn.

Schmaljohann 2019 already estimated species-specific random slopes linking migration start to arrival for 17 spring and 21 autumn songbird species and showed substantial among-species variation. PAYOFF-B therefore cannot claim novelty for beta_s itself or for heterogeneity in beta_s.
Franklin et al. 2022 meta-analyze within-stage repeatability across 47 species; that is not the same estimand as within-migration departure-to-arrival retention.
Ralston et al. 2025 explicitly identify individual migration distance as a candidate determinant of the ability to compensate delayed spring departure en route.

Comparative stopover studies show that long-distance migrants face stronger time constraints and make different departure decisions, but do not resolve whether migration distance strengthens or weakens departure-to-arrival timing retention at macroecological scale.

candidate_novel_estimand.name: migration_distance_modulation_of_timing_retention
candidate_novel_estimand.definition: beta_s remains the descriptive species-specific departure-to-arrival retention coordinate, but it is prior art. The candidate new test is whether species mean migration distance systematically predicts beta_s, i.e. whether longer journeys provide more opportunity to erase departure-time deviations or instead impose stronger time constraints that preserve them.

eligibility_gate.fail_if: Fewer than 20 species have >=8 individual-level paired records with nonzero within-stratum departure variation in at least one season.

preprocessing.date_coordinate: day-of-year on source migration year; no circular transformation unless source schema requires it
preprocessing.sex_handling: If sex is available, report sensitivity after subtracting sex-specific mean within eligible strata; do not select between versions by outcome.
preprocessing.no_outlier_trimming: No outcome-based trimming; only impossible dates or documented source errors may be excluded.

primary_analysis.model: One-stage multilevel moderation model on eligible individual-level spring records.
primary_analysis.response: arrival_anomaly centered within species x paper/study x tracking_year.
primary_analysis.focal_predictor: departure_anomaly centered in the same stratum.
distance_decomposition: between-species log migration distance = species mean log spring migration distance, standardized
within-species log migration distance = individual log spring migration distance minus species mean, standardized when informative
fixed_effects: departure_anomaly x between-species log migration distance [PRIMARY]
within-species log migration distance when sufficiently variable
departure_anomaly x within-species log migration distance [SECONDARY]
primary_analysis.primary_test: The coefficient of departure_anomaly x between-species log migration distance. This tests whether migration distance explains interspecific variation in the amount of departure timing retained to arrival.

competing_predictions.recourse_opportunity: negative interaction: longer-distance species compress a given departure deviation more strongly before arrival
competing_predictions.time_constraint: positive interaction: longer-distance species preserve/amplify a given departure deviation more strongly because schedules are tighter

secondary_outputs: species-specific shrunken retention slopes beta_s for visualization only; prior art, not novelty
spring-autumn contrast if the autumn eligibility gate independently passes
primary_analysis.interpretation: A null primary interaction closes the comparative route. Species-specific beta_s heterogeneity cannot rescue the paper because it is prior art.

moderator_analysis.primary_question: Does migration distance alter how strongly departure timing is retained to arrival?
competing_predictions: recourse-opportunity: longer routes offer more stages over which late individuals can accelerate or shorten stopovers, predicting lower beta_s
time-constraint: longer routes impose tighter schedules and less ability to absorb deviations, predicting higher beta_s
moderator_analysis.direction: two-sided because the two ecological mechanisms make opposing predictions.

admission_rule.data_gate: At least 20 species with >=8 informative paired individual records in spring after declared centering and nonzero departure variation.
admission_rule.distance_gate: At least 20 eligible species with nonmissing migration distance and sufficient between-species distance variation.
admission_rule.primary_success: The declared uncertainty interval for departure_anomaly x between-species log migration distance excludes zero.
admission_rule.secondary_only: Within-species distance interaction, spring-autumn contrast, and body mass cannot rescue a null primary distance interaction.
admission_rule.fail_closed: If any gate fails or the primary interaction is unresolved, close the comparative PAYOFF-B route without subgroup searches or threshold relaxation.

transparency: The Wang dataset has been used previously for pooled SEM; PAYOFF-B cannot claim discovery that departure predicts arrival.
No numerical timing values may be inspected before this contract is committed.
Schema probing may inspect file names, sheet names, headers and row counts only.

The contract was revised before Wang timing values were inspected because Schmaljohann 2019 was discovered to have already estimated species-specific start-to-arrival slopes. The revision narrows candidate novelty to ecological drivers of retention heterogeneity, principally migration distance.

After Ralston et al. 2025 was identified as explicitly proposing migration distance as a determinant of compensation after delayed departure, the final preoutcome model was changed from a two-stage beta_s meta-regression to the equivalent but more direct cross-level interaction departure_anomaly x migration_distance. No Wang timing outcomes had been inspected.
